acceptance: For every platform with registry category 'cloud' or a managed deployment mode, a non-interactive run without the acknowledgement exits with the documented code before an adapter is constructed; a test asserts no connection or credential lookup occurred, and a test enumerates the registry so a new cloud platform cannot be missed.
With the acknowledgement the run proceeds as today and the bundle's execution block records the acknowledgement and its source.
Local and self-hosted platforms, and interactive terminal runs, behave as before; tests cover each.

The same rule applies to compare when it runs platforms. Local-mode MCP run_benchmark refuses a billable platform unless the operator allowed it at server start; a test proves no tool argument can grant it. Remote mode keeps its existing allow-list behaviour.
The PR lists every in-repository caller checked (the UAT matrix, workflows, live tests) and updates any that the change breaks; the changelog.d fragment marks the change as breaking.

The PR carries the coverage table described above, and states whether an agent can submit to or publish the results corpus without a human step. Anything found outside this item's scope is listed for the owner, not fixed here.

Help text and documentation state the rule and its limits: a caller can set the acknowledgement itself, and platform credentials kept in the user's BenchBox credentials file are readable by any process the user runs.
context:
Origin: adversarial review on 2026-11-13 of work first left unfiled. The earlier reasons assumed a person at the keyboard; this item records the corrected disposition. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Evidence: the confirmation is guarded by 'sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty() and not s.non_interactive'. A search of the CLI and MCP code found no spend, budget or billable guard on run.

Decision gates (settle in the PR description before coding): (1) the acknowledgement's form. Default: an environment variable plus an equivalent CLI flag, with the environment variable the only form MCP accepts at server start. (2) What counts as billable is decided: registry category 'cloud' or managed deployment mode; list every affected platform in the PR. (3) The exit code. Follow the table set by compare-exit-codes-distinct-outcomes-20261112 if it has landed; otherwise choose an unused code and record it there. If the resolved deployment mode is not known before adapter construction, stop and report; do not move the check after the connection.

Validator notes. Guaranteed invariant: no non-interactive managed run starts without an acknowledgement in the invocation or environment. False negatives: a caller that sets the acknowledgement itself; a billable service reached through a self-hosted mode. False positives: free-tier managed runs. Maintenance trigger: every new platform or deployment mode.

Verification rubric: pass only if the refusal is proven to precede any connection, the MCP argument test exists, and no live-cloud run was used to test it.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. Related items are delivered together on one feature branch and one PR, as their umbrella item names (site work: BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site); squash-merged. Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.

Revision (2026-11-13), after an independent critique and owner decisions: priority lowered to medium: credentials must already be configured by a person, and nothing in this repository was found to break. The critique reported that nightly cloud jobs run pytest suites rather than the CLI and that the UAT matrix pins self-hosted modes; re-verify both. It also reported that platform credentials are stored in plaintext under ~/.benchbox/credentials.yaml (benchbox/security/credentials.py) and that the keyring holds only the submit token; verify before documenting.

Closeout (2026-11-13): delivered by https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/pull/4203, merged to develop as 5ba48a6796, with the external reviewer's SHIP and no open findings on head 862158097e. Checked on origin/develop: the billable-platform guard modules, the host_load block in benchbox/core/results/environment.py and the exit-code table are present. The delivering agent reported: compare exits 0/1/2/3/4 on a real bundle smoke; results validate exits 5 on FAIL and matches the MCP tool; the guard exits 6 before any credential read or connection, MCP accepts it only from the environment at server start, dry-run is exempt; host load is recorded at start and end, null for DataFrame adapters, which never took the snapshot. One required CI job failed once on an unrelated UAT timing test and passed on rerun. For the owner: the validator fails 89 of 491 published bundles, 74 of them ranking-eligible (mostly SF1 row counts and required keys; BigQuery and Snowflake 25 each); run --dry-run still reads credentials and may make network calls; platform credentials are stored in plaintext in ~/.benchbox/credentials.yaml; publish and submit ask no confirmation once a destination or token exists; run-official can acknowledge only via the environment variable; site documentation for the exit codes, validate command, guard and host-load fields is not yet written (text is in the PR body).
description:
Problem: the only check before benchbox run executes is the 'Proceed with execution?' prompt, shown only when stdin and stdout are terminals and --non-interactive is not set (benchbox/cli/commands/run.py). An agent or CI job therefore reaches a billable cloud platform with no check. Local MCP runs are non-interactive by nature; MCP remote mode already refuses platforms outside the operator's allowed_platforms (benchbox/mcp/security.py).

Owner decision (2026-11-13): refuse, in both CLI and MCP. A platform is billable when the platform registry gives it category 'cloud' or the resolved deployment mode is 'managed'. An earlier definition by managed deployment mode alone was wrong: most cloud platforms, including Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks and Redshift, declare no deployment mode.

Outcome: in non-interactive mode a billable run refuses to start without an explicit acknowledgement, before any credential read or connection, with a documented exit code. For local MCP, reuse the allow-list mechanism: the default allows local platforms only, and the operator opts cloud platforms in when starting the server; no tool argument can grant it. The bundle records the acknowledgement and its source.

Also in scope (merged from noninteractive-safeguard-audit-20261113): a coverage table in the PR listing every CLI command and non-read-only MCP tool that can start a platform, publish, submit, delete or install, and what each does without a terminal.

Non-goals: interactive behaviour; cost estimation; budget caps; fixing other commands found by the coverage table (list them for the owner).
